clue.text: Funny man using martial art on clergyman

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places one part after the other, so the art comes first and the clergyman follows

blocks.note: kendo is the Japanese art of fencing with bamboo swords
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a title held by senior clergy

explanation.surface: A comedian performs his act armed with a martial art against a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a famous Liverpool comedian with wild hair and a feather duster.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Dodd was a celebrated British stand-up comedian, so he is a classic example of a funny man.

clue.text: "You can see with this!", I shout to the auditor

indicators.note: an auditor here is a listener, so the words are judged by how they come across when spoken

blocks.note: to bawl is to shout loudly

explanation.surface: Someone yells at an accountant that the evidence is right there to be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant checking books, but it means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyeball is the organ of sight, literally the thing a person looks through.

clue.text: Start to eat and drink after I'd given up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read from the bottom, so the two letters run backwards
the drink is placed following the other part in the answer

blocks.note: the contraction taken letter for letter
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into food and drink after quitting a bad habit.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig in is an informal phrasal verb meaning to begin eating heartily.

clue.text: Carroll really has to avoid losing last child

indicators.note: losing its last means the final letter of the avoiding word is dropped

blocks.note: to dodge is to avoid
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll must steer clear of losing his last child, a nod to his fondness for young friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of Charles Dodgson, so 'really' points to his true surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland wrote under a pseudonym; his actual family name was this.

clue.text: Paths laid out round a large pitch

indicators.note: laid out means arranged afresh, so these letters are set in a new order
round means surrounding, so the remaining pieces sit inside the rearranged ones

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Footpaths are marked out around a big sports field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like a playing field, matching the paths, but it is the black tarry substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is a bitumen mixture, and pitch is a similar dark tarry material used for surfacing roads.

clue.text: Saw, for example, in front of garage

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: say is used to introduce an example
taken as written
the opening letter of garage

explanation.surface: A saw is offered as an example of a tool found in a garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the cutting tool kept in a garage; here it means an old maxim.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, which is exactly what a saying is.

clue.text: Here Flora preserved the metal she has...

blocks.note: the object form of she
barium is a soft metallic element

explanation.surface: A woman named Flora keeps the metal she owns somewhere safe, and the story continues in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Flora is not a woman but plant life; the clue reads 'she has' as HER coming before the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbarium is a collection of dried, pressed plant specimens, a place where a region's plants are kept.

clue.text: ... to start with metal not available...

blocks.note: lead is a heavy grey metal
a dish that is off is no longer on the menu

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the metal is out of stock from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead off is to begin or open proceedings, the first one to go.

clue.text: Speaking slightingly of mad gent and praise eccentrically

indicators.note: acting eccentrically means behaving oddly, so the letters are arranged in an unexpected way

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A dotty gentleman and some odd praise make for a backhanded compliment.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparagement is the act of belittling, talking about someone in a derogatory, dismissive way.

clue.text: Composer given introductions to Busoni, Elgar, Ravel and Grieg

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so the opening letter of each name is kept

blocks.note: the first letters of the four composers' names

explanation.surface: A composer is presented alongside four famous fellow composers.
explanation.walkthrough: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School, best known for the opera Wozzeck.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg wrote operas and concertos in the twentieth century, making him a noted composer.

clue.text: Newspaper getting money that's prayed for

blocks.note: a daily is a paper published every day
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: A newspaper receives cash that someone has been hoping for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give us this day our daily bread' is a line of the Lord's Prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord's Prayer asks for sustenance in these words, so it is literally requested in prayer.

clue.text: County containing upper-class resorts

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county on the south coast
U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: An English county is full of posh seaside holiday towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resorts' looks like a noun for holiday towns but is used in the sense of favourite places one returns to.
explanation.definitionFit: Haunts are places frequently visited, and resorts in an older sense are places habitually gone to.

clue.text: Write to nag about military headquarters

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are turned into a fresh order

blocks.note: to pen is to write
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone sends a complaining letter to the army's headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentagon in Virginia houses the United States Department of Defense, the American armed forces' command centre.

clue.text: Dread sex manual translated from French author

indicators.note: a translation turns words into another form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A frightful guide to lovemaking has been rendered into English from a French writer.
explanation.definitionFit: He wrote The Three Musketeers and The Count of Monte Cristo, among the most famous French novels.

clue.text: English phone box designed for one who won't speak to the French?

definitions.text: one who won't speak to the French?

indicators.note: something designed is newly made up, so these letters are put into another arrangement

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An English phone box built for a person who refuses to call France.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that refusing to speak to the French is just one example of fearing foreigners.
explanation.definitionFit: A xenophobe dislikes or fears foreigners, so shunning French people is one illustration of the attitude.

clue.text: Moment that's doubtful on the first of January

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept from the month
in an across clue the doubtful word is placed next to the remaining letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of the month's name
iffy is informal for uncertain

explanation.surface: A moment of uncertainty on New Year's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first of January' looks like a date but just means its initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A jiffy is an informal word for a very short time, an instant.

clue.text: Wood has award sent back to New York

indicators.note: sent back means returned, so the award is read from right to left
to here means attached to, so the city's letters follow on

blocks.note: OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
standard abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A woodworker returns a British honour and moves to New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a dense black hardwood from tropical trees, prized for carving and piano keys.

clue.text: Favourable comment elicited by the scent of wine?

blocks.note: first meaning: a compliment
second meaning: the aroma given off by a wine

explanation.surface: A wine taster praises the aroma of the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a compliment, praise handed out like flowers, and the characteristic aroma of a vintage.

clue.text: A Greek king soon brought about plucky Ilium's end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing letter, so only that is taken from the city's name
brought about means placed around, so the first piece wraps the others

blocks.note: anon is an old word for soon
game means brave and willing
the closing letter of Ilium

explanation.surface: A Greek king will soon bring about the downfall of brave Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ilium is the Latin name for Troy, which Agamemnon led the Greeks to destroy; the whole of 'A Greek king' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was king of Mycenae and commander of the Greek forces in the Trojan War.

clue.text: Extra cover for porky dramatist

indicators.note: a cover goes around what it protects, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: more means additional
porky is rhyming slang for a lie, from pork pie

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at extra cover is a plump playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Extra cover is a cricket fielding position, which the surface leans on; porky (pork pie) is British rhyming slang for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the great seventeenth-century French playwright, author of Tartuffe and The Miser.

clue.text: Speech made by opposition leader on official allowance

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is taken
in a down clue the first part sits on top of the second

blocks.note: the opening letter of opposition
a ration is a fixed official allowance of food

explanation.surface: The leader of the opposition gives a speech about state allowances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposition leader' suggests a politician but just yields the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal address delivered to an audience, a grand piece of public speaking.

clue.text: Beautiful young women serving time on islands

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits above the second

blocks.note: an hour is a period of time
Is is the abbreviation for islands

explanation.surface: Pretty young women are doing a stint of work on some islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Houris are the beautiful virgins of Islamic paradise, and by extension any alluring young women.

clue.text: Persistently question North African about where medicinal waters are dispensed

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the North African is read backwards

blocks.note: to pump someone is to quiz them for information
a Moor is a person from north-west Africa

explanation.surface: Someone grills a North African about the location of a spa's healing springs.
explanation.walkthrough: A pump room is the hall at a spa town such as Bath where mineral water is served.
explanation.definitionFit: Pump rooms at spa resorts were built so visitors could drink the supposedly healing mineral water.

clue.text: Like Croesus completely, Diana only partly

indicators.note: only partly means just a portion is used, so the answer lies within the run of words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and into the next

explanation.surface: A comparison with the rich king Croesus fits one person completely and Diana only in part.
explanation.walkthrough: Croesus was the famously wealthy king of Lydia, in what is now Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Croesus ruled the ancient kingdom of Lydia, so the adjective for its people describes him.

clue.text: See 14
It's too far away from the stove

blocks.note: first meaning: beyond the distance something can reach
second meaning: taken out of a cooker, a range being a kitchen stove

explanation.surface: Something sits too far from the cooker to be reached.
explanation.walkthrough: A range is a large kitchen stove, so the second reading is food lifted off it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means beyond reach or shot, and literally means removed from a cooking range.

clue.text: Muses initially help poetic young woman

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of Muses
aid means help

explanation.surface: The Muses first come to the aid of a young woman writing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poetic' marks this as a literary word for a girl, as in maid of honour or Maid Marian.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid is an old-fashioned, chiefly literary word for a girl or unmarried woman.

clue.text: One who doesn't believe he is in a race

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these words go within the race

blocks.note: taken as written
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A non-believer claims he is taking part in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist rejects belief in any god, so is a person without religious faith.

clue.text: Almost half of retailers imported wrong wine

indicators.note: almost half means a little under half the word survives, the rest being cut off
imported means brought in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the word whose front part is kept
a sin is a moral wrong

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers have brought in the wrong bottles of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Retailers has nine letters, so its first four, a little under half, are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.
